action: A close-up giraffe head tilts its muzzle up and to the right, opens its mouth, then pulls the muzzle back and settles with the mouth slightly open.
identity_gap: Construction and viewpoint: the doodle is a side-profile giraffe built from about a dozen straight strokes (long neck, box muzzle, loop/P ossicones, no spots or ears), while the cartoon is a cropped three-quarter head close-up with ears, spots and dense broken contour lines that read as edges traced from a photo.
notes: Frames 1-3 read as one continuous muzzle lift; at 4-5 the muzzle shrinks and redraws in a different shape with gray ghost lines of a larger muzzle, and 6-8 are nearly static. Only the ossicone loops loosely echo the doodle; nothing else carries its stroke habits or simplifications.
